body: Spool keeps only SessionStart and SessionEnd (ids, pids, folder, transcript path; no prompt or answer text). Turn answers (Stop), prompts and subagent events of a period without hub stay lost as today. Alternative: spool every event with free text stripped, or keep Stop answers (late answers out of order, text on disk).

One file per event under <state>/spool/<session>/<nanos>-<event_id>.json written as .tmp and renamed (maildir); the file keeps the HookPost with its event_id so the hub's dedup drops a copy. Alternative: one appended jsonl per session (needs a cross-process lock; a partial line or a concurrent delete loses events).

Replay is per session: every hook of the session replays its spool first (stops at the first failure, own event then kept or dropped, never sent ahead), and the agent replays its session's spool after every registration. Alternative: hook-only replay (an idle session stays invisible until the next prompt) or a device-wide replay of all sessions (cross-session races, stale starts of dead sessions could create topics).

Replay and the own POST share one deadline = the event's existing POST timeout, so a down hub costs a hook no more than before (SessionEnd budget unchanged). Alternative: a separate replay budget (up to 2x the timeout inside SessionEnd's shared 1.5 s).

Device state dir = absolute CCTG_STATE_DIR (process env or device.env), else <home>/.cctg; a relative value is ignored because hooks run in the session folder. Alternative: honour relative values like the hub does (spool would land inside project folders).

Soak simulates Claude Code with stand-in processes named claude.exe (a copy of the soak test binary) started through a launcher that exits, so the real cctg hook walks a real process tree: top-level stand-ins end the chain, the nested stand-in is a child of A1. Hooks and agents are children of their stand-in (agent Register.claude_pid = hook claude_pid). Alternative: inject HookPosts directly (skips the hook binary and the nesting walk) or spawn hooks from the test (under Claude Code every hook would see the orchestrator's claude as its own).

Soak is a harness=false test target that runs only with -- --ignored and otherwise prints 'skipped'; the same binary re-executes itself as launcher/stand-in by env role. Alternative: libtest #[ignore] plus re-exec through a test filter (libtest writes to stdout, which the stand-in protocol uses).

A burst of tool-call lines only does not build a queue the permission prompt can overtake: the scheduler merges consecutive tool lines of a topic into one message when more wait than tokens, so 60 tool lines drained in a few sends. The soak burst therefore uses typed prompts (never merged) plus tool lines.
Counting the A #2 stream lines sent after its permission prompt right when the prompt went out gave 0 (they had not been sent yet); the count is taken after the burst drained.

Spool cross-process race: kept lock-free with a documented bounded-overshoot rule (each concurrent saver adds at most its own file past a cap; k savers -> at most k-1 extra files of <=16 KiB, next save sees Full), proven by a concurrent-save unit test. Alternative rejected: a create_new lock file with stale-lock recovery (adds a wait inside the hook budget and a stale-lock failure mode for a bound that only limits disk use).

cctg-test-*-slots leak: reproduced 12 leaked dirs (registry.json only) in 8 ordinary lib runs and 20 more from one killed run. Fixed in the test-only TempDir: Drop retries remove_dir_all until the dir is gone (nothing recreates it: RegistryStore::save never creates dirs) and the first TempDir of a run sweeps cctg-test-* older than 1 h (killed runs). Alternative rejected: Rig::shutdown awaited in ~75 slots tests plus a production saver handle; it does not cover killed runs and costs far more diff.

Live soak keeps polling getUpdates (OPEN_DECISIONS: user hub stopped, one consumer) so it can verify forum_topic_edited deletion in its own topics; foreign service messages are filtered out of the check and the hub never deletes them (slot_by_topic). Alternative rejected: PLAN_V2 no-polling live mode, which cannot check the acceptance line about service messages on the real group.

Splitting the 560-line soak scenario into phase functions (PLAN_V2 finding 12) rejected: the phases share about 20 locals (sims, topic ids, latencies, notes), a context struct would add code without changing coverage, and a panic-safe task wrapper already bounds failure cleanup.

Tried to reproduce a cross-session spool race (prune of one save removing another session's fresh empty dir between its create_dir_all and create_new, losing a SessionStart) with 2 and 8 concurrent savers x 1500-3000 rounds on Windows: 0 lost of 18000 saves. Not reported as a defect.

Fake soak 429s are armed after both permission prompts were sent, with offsets [2, 6] into the rest of the burst, plus an assertion that both fired before the burst drained, so the recorded permission latency never includes a 429 pause and 429 coverage stays in the burst. Alternative rejected: the review's verbatim move keeping offsets [3, 12] after the prompts, which risks the second 429 spilling into phase 5 or not firing, since merged stream messages after the prompts are few and uncounted.

Live soak counts pending updates with one getUpdates without offset before the hub starts (confirms nothing; count only, capped at 100 by Telegram) and documents the preconditions in docs/soak.md. Alternative rejected: starting the poll from the real hub's persisted offset, which needs reading the user's state dir and still consumes the same updates.

Permission-priority mutation (next_permission -> None) on the post-fix soak is first caught by the 'both planned 429s fell into the burst' check, not by the permission assertion; to prove the permission assertion is not vacuous the mutation was re-run with that check neutralised (Q3), and it failed at 'the prompt of A2 overtook stream lines'. Alternative: accept the side-effect kill as proof.
